title: End a purchase the network never answered

blocks.text: The acquirer forwards Mastercard purchases to the network with `QueryHost`. Cardholders write in: the terminal said the purchase failed, they paid again another way, and their bank still shows a hold for the first attempt. On the same days, a few terminals waited their full timeout and got nothing at all. The Mastercard link also goes down for maintenance now and then.

`AfterNetwork` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/AfterNetwork.java` stands right after `QueryHost` in the `mastercard` group. After the group the chain has an abort participant that answers reported failures (as in the unit) and `SendResponse`. Finish `prepare`, marked `TODO`, so that every purchase ends with the right answer at the terminal and nothing left wrong at the network. Something else sends what you put on the `saf` queue, and `reversalOf` builds the message. About eight lines.

The tests deploy a real TransactionManager, a real `QueryHost` and two real QMUXes with Q2, in the test's own JVM. A scripted network on the far side approves, declines or never answers. One QMUX's link is down.

cases.says: the network's approval reaches the terminal and leaves nothing to put right
a purchase the network never answered fails as unreachable (91), not as a decline
a purchase the network received but never answered leaves one reversal pointing at it
a decline from the network is an answer: it goes to the terminal and needs no reversal
a purchase that was never sent because the link was down leaves nothing to reverse

origin.section: 5.6 A Network That Doesn't Answer Has Not Declined

concepts: Only a request the network received can need a reversal: a silent network does, a decline or a down link doesn't.
With continuations, QueryHost resumes a timed-out transaction as prepared with no response; a participant after it must fail the transaction so the terminal gets 91.
